guidance: The command argument is the exact program invocation to execute. Repeat it exactly as written.
Do not substitute a workload description, add cd/setup wrappers, change python/python3, or infer a different command from surrounding context.

nodes.guidance: Express the node count clearly enough to recover the expected numeric value.

tasks.guidance: Express the task count clearly enough to recover the expected numeric value.

working_directory.guidance: Working directories are paths; preserve the expected working_directory exactly.

guidance: Slurm scheduler/resource arguments such as nodes, tasks, and working_directory are separate tool arguments. They are not part of command unless already present in the expected command string.

run_info_json.guidance: run_info_json is a literal JSON string argument. Preserve that string exactly when it is included in a generated prompt.

blocking.guidance: Express whether the Slurm job submission should block clearly enough to recover the expected boolean value.

nodes.guidance: Express the node count clearly enough to recover the expected numeric value.

tasks.guidance: Express the task count clearly enough to recover the expected numeric value.

time_limit.guidance: Express the Slurm time limit clearly enough to recover the expected value; exact spelling is helpful but not required.

account.guidance: Slurm account names are identifiers; preserve the expected account exactly.

partition.guidance: Slurm partition names are identifiers; preserve the expected partition exactly.

exclusive.guidance: Express whether exclusive nodes should be requested clearly enough to recover the expected boolean value.

cpus_per_task.guidance: Express CPUs per task clearly enough to recover the expected numeric value.

job_name_prefix.guidance: Job name prefixes are identifiers; preserve the expected job_name_prefix exactly.

guidance: For Slurm submit_jobs, run_info_json describes generated runs while scheduler options such as blocking, nodes, tasks, time_limit, account, partition, exclusive, cpus_per_task, and job_name_prefix are separate submit_jobs arguments.

job_set_id.guidance: job_set_id is the local MADA job-set identifier. Do not replace it with slurm_job_id.

slurm_job_id.guidance: slurm_job_id is the real Slurm scheduler job identifier. Do not replace it with job_set_id.

job_set_id.guidance: job_set_id is the local MADA job-set identifier. Do not replace it with slurm_job_id.

slurm_job_id.guidance: slurm_job_id is the real Slurm scheduler job identifier. Do not replace it with job_set_id.

wait_until.guidance: wait_until is an enum-like status target; preserve the expected value exactly.

poll_interval_seconds.guidance: Express the polling interval clearly enough to recover the expected numeric seconds value.

timeout_seconds.guidance: Express the timeout clearly enough to recover the expected numeric seconds value.

guidance: For Slurm continuous status checks, the prompt should imply repeated monitoring until the expected wait_until condition or timeout.
